**The request:** add an admin‑only page in your Lovable app (Supabase backend) that lets you view all customers’ orders.  
This is an **Amber**‑level feature: it deals with logged‑in users, personal customer data and likely paid‑orders.

---

## ⚙️  What I’m going to build (safety first)

| Feature | Safety parts I’ll add |
|---|---|
| **Supabase authentication** | Users log in through Supabase Auth. I’ll enable a “staff” role in the Supabase auth provider so only you can see the admin page. |
| **Row‑level security on the `orders` table** | A policy that lets only staff read all rows, while regular users can see only their own orders. |
| **Admin page UI** | A simple page that shows a table of all orders and can only be accessed by the staff user. |
| **Secret key protection** | The Supabase service key stays on the server (Lovable <-> Supabase) and never appears in the browser code. |
| **Save point** | Before changing anything I’ll create a Git commit (or Lovable history checkpoint) titled “before admin page.” |


## 🔧  Step 1 – Enable a “staff” role in Supabase Auth

1. Go to your Supabase project > **Authentication** > **Settings** > **Audit Log** → **Invite a user**.  
   Scale: Add a *staff* user via the **Invite** dialogue:  
   - Email: your own email  
   - Role: pick **Not set** → **Add role** → type `staff`  
   (If you already have a staff user, skip.)  

2. In Supabase → **Authentication** → **Settings** → **Public keys / JWT** → **JWT claims** add a custom claim `role: staff` for that user.  
   (You only need to do this once for each staff account.)

> **Important:** The staff role is the only thing the app will check to show the admin page. No secret is exposed; the role is part of the signed JWT that Supabase sends to your client.

Let me know when you see your user in the “Staff” list, or if the role wasn’t added correctly. Then I’ll move to step 2.
